facts.fact_text: On 6 May 2012 a public demonstration entitled the 'March of Millions' was held in central Moscow.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 was held to protest against the allegedly rigged presidential elections.
The 'March of Millions' demonstration on 6 May 2012 had been approved by the Moscow city authorities in the form of a march followed by a meeting at Bolotnaya Square.
The march on 6 May 2012 was peaceful and held without any disruptions.
The applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) took part in the demonstration on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the first applicant (Mr Asainov), on 6 May 2012 he had arrived at Bolotnaya Square to take part in the peaceful demonstration.
According to the first applicant (Mr Asainov), before his arrest on 6 May 2012 he had not committed any breach of public order or other offences.
According to the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) wife, she had come to take part in the authorised demonstration at Bolotnaya Square with her husband on 6 May 2012.
According to the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) wife, she and her husband passed Yakimanka Street together with other participants of the demonstration on 6 May 2012.
According to the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), she arrived at Oktyabrskaya metro station at 4 p.m. on 6 May 2012 to take part in the peaceful demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.

According to the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), she passed Yakimanka Street with other participants of the demonstration on 6 May 2012, but on approaching Bolotnaya Square found the entrance blocked.
According to the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), she did not breach public order and had not taken part in any acts of violence prior to her arrest on 6 May 2012.
There were numerous clashes between the police and protesters at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.

When the marchers arrived at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, it transpired that barriers installed by the police had narrowed the entrance to the meeting venue, allegedly restricting the space allocated for the meeting.
To control the crowd at Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012, a police cordon forced the protestors to remain within the barriers.
At 5.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police ordered that the meeting at Bolotnaya Square finish early and began to disperse the participants.
It took the police about two hours to clear the protestors from Bolotnaya Square on 6 May 2012.
The applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were arrested at the venue of the demonstration on 6 May 2012 at Bolotnaya Square.
After their arrest, the applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were taken to police stations.
At the police stations, the applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were charged with administrative offences.
The applicants (Mr Asainov and Ms Sibiryak) were convicted of administrative offences as charged by the justices of the peace.
According to the first applicant (Mr Asainov), around 8.55 p.m. on 6 May 2012 he had been arrested outside the venue of the demonstration at Bolotnaya Square.
According to the first applicant (Mr Asainov), before his arrest on 6 May 2012 he had not received any orders from the police.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Asainov), as a participant in the authorised demonstration on 6 May 2012, had broken through the police cordon and tried to pass to Red Square.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had ignored the police orders to cease his actions of breaking through the police cordon on 6 May 2012.
According to the Government, the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had actively resisted the police officers while being taken to the police van on 6 May 2012.
At 8.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the first applicant (Mr Asainov) was brought to the Fili-Davydkovo district police station in Moscow.

At the Fili-Davydkovo district police station, an on-duty officer drew up a record of the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) administrative escorting for the purpose of compiling an administrative file.
The administrative arrest record for the first applicant (Mr Asainov) indicated that he had been arrested at 8.30 p.m. at the Fili-Davydkovo district police station on 6 May 2012.
The administrative arrest record for the first applicant (Mr Asainov) indicated that he had been released at 11.05 p.m. on 6 May 2012.
A duty officer at the Fili-Davydkovo district police station drew up an administrative offence record in respect of the first applicant (Mr Asainov).
The administrative offence record stated that on 6 May 2012 at 8.30 p.m. at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow the first applicant (Mr Asainov) took part in an authorised meeting.
The administrative offence record stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) broke through the police cordon and tried to enter Red Square, pushing police officers away.

The administrative offence record stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) did not react to the multiple lawful demands of the police to cease these actions and actively resisted while being taken to the police van.

The administrative offence record stated that the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) conduct was in breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, demonstrating his refusal to obey the lawful orders of the police officers and preventing them from fulfilling their service duties.
On 29 May 2012 the Justice of the Peace of circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow examined the administrative charges against the first applicant (Mr Asainov) in his presence.

On the basis of the statements of two police officers, the Justice of the Peace of circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow established that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had committed an administrative offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, as described in the administrative offence record.
The first applicant (Mr Asainov) was sentenced by the Justice of the Peace of circuit no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow to a fine of 500 Russian roubles (about EUR 12 at the time).
The first applicant (Mr Asainov) appealed against the judgment of the Justice of the Peace to the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.

On 16 July 2012 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow examined and partly granted the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) request to exclude the written statements of the police officers as inadmissible evidence.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow summoned the police officers to be examined at the hearing as witnesses.
On 2 August 2012 the hearing at the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow was adjourned to 23 August 2012.
The first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) request to be represented by one more lawyer was granted by the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.
The first applicant (Mr Asainov) and his lawyer were duly summoned to the hearing scheduled for 23 August 2012 at the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow.

On 22 August 2012 the first applicant (Mr Asainov) sent a telegram to the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow asking to adjourn the hearing on the grounds that he was away from Moscow for family reasons.
On 23 August 2012 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow held a hearing in the absence of the first applicant (Mr Asainov) and his lawyers.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow mentioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing that none of the first applicant (Mr Asainov) or his lawyers had lodged a request to adjourn the hearing.
At the 23 August 2012 hearing, the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow questioned two police officers.

The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov), together with other participants of the demonstration, had pushed through the police cordon and tried to approach the Kremlin.
The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had pushed the police officers away.
The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had thrown stones, glass bottles and smoke bombs.
The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had disregarded multiple demands by the police to cease his actions.
The two police officers questioned at the 23 August 2012 hearing stated that the first applicant (Mr Asainov) had resisted arrest.
The appeal decision of the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow of 23 August 2012 did not mention the eye-witness statement submitted by the first applicant's (Mr Asainov's) wife.

Relying on the testimony of the two police officers, the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow upheld the first-instance judgment convicting the first applicant (Mr Asainov) of an administrative offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
According to the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), around 6.30 p.m. on 6 May 2012 the police started to break the crowd up into groups and push them.
According to the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), two police officers grabbed her hands and pushed her towards the police van on 6 May 2012.
According to the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), at around 9.05 p.m. on 6 May 2012 she was brought to Khoroshevskiy district police station.

According to the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), after the police drew up an administrative offence record at Khoroshevskiy district police station, she was released at around 1.40 a.m. on 7 May 2012.

According to the Government, the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) had disregarded the police order to cease breaking through the police cordon and to disperse.
According to the Government, the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) was taken to the police station at 8.10 p.m. on 6 May 2012.
According to the Government, the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) was released at 10.35 p.m. on 6 May 2012.

The logbook of persons brought to the Khoroshevskiy district police station indicated that the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) was released at 10.35 p.m. on 6 May 2012.
The administrative file for the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) contained no record of her being escorted to the Khoroshevskiy district police station.

The record of administrative arrest for the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak), compiled at 8.20 p.m. on 6 May 2012, indicated that she had been taken to the Khoroshevskiy district police station at 8.10 p.m. and released later on the same day.
The second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) was accused of having disobeyed a lawful police order, which was an offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The administrative offence record for the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) stated that on 6 May 2012 at 7.15 p.m. she took part in an authorised meeting at Bolotnaya Square in Moscow.
The administrative offence record for the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) stated that she broke through the police cordon and tried to approach the Kremlin.

The administrative offence record for the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) stated that she did not react to the multiple lawful demands of the police officers to cease these actions, thereby preventing them from fulfilling their service duties, in breach of Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The administrative case-file for the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) contained a police officer's report which was drawn up on a template.
The police officer's report in the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) administrative case-file contained no individualised information except the police officer's and the applicant's personal data.

The police officer's report in the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) administrative case-file substantially repeated the description of the applicant's acts contained in the administrative offence record.
The police officer's report in the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) administrative case-file added that the applicant had thrown stones at the police, lit fireworks and resisted arrest.
On 30 May 2012 the Justice of the Peace of Circuit Court no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow examined the administrative charges against the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak).

The second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) was not present at the 30 May 2012 hearing before the Justice of the Peace of Circuit Court no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow, even though she had been summoned to attend.

On the basis of the police officer's report, the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) was found guilty under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences by the Justice of the Peace of Circuit Court no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow.
The second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) was sentenced by the Justice of the Peace of Circuit Court no. 100 of the Yakimanka District of Moscow to a fine of 500 Russian roubles (about EUR 12 at the time).
On 13 November 2012 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow examined the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) appeal in her presence.

On 13 November 2012 the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow upheld the first-instance judgment convicting the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) of an administrative offence under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.

The second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) request to have the police officers who had arrested her examined at the 13 November 2012 hearing before the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow was dismissed.
At the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) request, the Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow examined a witness of defence at the 13 November 2012 hearing.
The defence witness at the 13 November 2012 hearing stated that the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) had not participated in breaking through the police cordon and had not committed any unlawful acts.
The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow dismissed the defence witness's statements as unreliable evidence on the grounds that he was the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) friend.

The Zamoskvoretskiy District Court of Moscow considered that the second applicant (Ms Sibiryak) had been duly summoned to the first-instance hearing by telephone but had failed to appear or to lodge a request for its adjournment.
On 15 April 2013 the Deputy President of the Moscow City Court examined the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) administrative case in supervisory review proceedings.
On 15 April 2013 the Deputy President of the Moscow City Court upheld the earlier judicial decisions in the second applicant's (Ms Sibiryak's) administrative case.
